Intermediate Summoner

Hi, are you familiar yet with pet raising and sweets box? If not, please read it on the basics!

Class Combination

Summoner has 4 viable subclasses: the common Fighter and Phantom, and the more niche Braver and Bouncer:

  • SuFi: Most common combination. Best combination if Ph is not yet available
  • SuPh: The premier combo for everything. It is stronger than SuFi with great PP regeneration, but requires the character to have 200 PP
  • SuBr: Great for beginners, especially players new to Summoner and new to PSO2
  • SuBo: Has good PP regen and strong against breakable parts, but difficult to use.

All multipliers listed are not counting High Level Bonus, which is a must-take. The "Damage Rating" stated is based on critical builds, whose explanation can be found after this section.

Summoner-Fighter (SuFi)

Recommended for all skill levels. SuFi has the highest stance multiplier and less likely need to switch stance, but offers little compensation once PP runs out and has lowest critical rate (means your base damage will be lower). Despite this, SuFi remains well-rounded and is a good choice towards end-game, especially if Phantom is not available.

Summoner-Phantom (SuPh)

The final destination of Summoner. SuPh has high multiplier, high PP regeneration, and no stances, making it easy to use. In every way, compared to other subs, Ph stands superior as an all rounder. However, it requires 200 PP to be effective, 2 level 75 classes to unlock Ph, and Ph weaponry to sustain its leveling since Ph cannot have a subclass.

Summoner-Luster (SuLu)

An alternative to SuPh, mainly if you are confident in your ability to keep attacking your target. Luster sub heavily relies on the combo count, or voltage, to do proper damage since the more combo you do, the more critical rate you have. You'll need both Shinkuro and Zanverse to keep your damage up.

Summoner-Braver (SuBr)

Recommended for beginners. SuBr has the easiest usage, but relatively lacks output. This is compensated by Attack Advance which, on several pets, provides a PA-powered normal attacks with 0 PP usage. This contributes to its beginner-friendly nature as newbies tend to use normal attacks a lot. SuBr is best when fighting bosses whose weak point is exposed for a long time to warrant Weak Stance activation, such as Dark Falz Elder, Cuento Dragon, Dark Falz Persona, Demoire Dominus, and Veiled Fordruss.

Property Description
Damage rating 154.06% (Average Stance with Attack Advance), 180.86% (Weak Stance with Attack Advance)[#sub-damage-calculation Explanation]

Ease of use Easy
Best compatibility Rappy. If your Rappy has Spirited Parfait (はりきりパフェ), you can just use normal attacks since it will become Rappy's top DPS move, being only slightly (~5%) less powerful than Rappy End with S Charge.

Summoner-Bouncer (SuBo)

SuBo has a superior PP regeneration mechanism. They are the only sub-class that allows Summonner to reach 100% critical without external help (means your base damage is all-time highest). While it does not have high multiplier compared to Fi, its PP regeneration is more than enough to make it up, even with only Elemental Stance; this means that you will need to get used to PA constantly. Unfortunately, using SuBo means you require extra palette slot to accommodate Fields, and you will be required to maintain your Shifta and Deband. SuBo is best when fighting bosses whose break point is exposed for a long time to warrant Break Stance activation, such as Dark/Omega Falz Luther, Profound/Unfathomable Darkness, Magatsu, Quent Dragon, and Dark Falz Persona.

Other Class Combinations

Other than Fi, Ph, Br, and Bo, no other class combination works for Su:

Sub Multiplier with Critical Ring
Hunter 115.71%
Force 110.51%
Force (Photon Flare) 120.92%
Techer (Elemental Weak) 137.61%
Etoile 143.67%
Etoile (Tech Attack Count Bonus) 165.22%
  • Su doesn't have JA, which means SuHu and SuEt will not work well:
    • SuHu gains nothing from JA Bonus; Fury Stance only boost Striking and Ranged while all Pet attacks are considered Tech (regardless of Switch skills)
    • SuEt cannot activate Flat Attack bonus because this skill only applies to missing JA on attacks that have JA. Pet attacks have no JA
    • SuEt doesn't gain any critical rate from Etoile tree, making its base damage lower.
    • SuEt with Tech Attack Count Bonus is incompatible with a lot of pets' combo which involve using a single attack repeatedly
  • Pet attacks, while always do Tech damage, is not a Technic:
    • Elemental Mastery (e.g. Fire Mastery, Light Mastery, etc.) skills are invalid due to only working for Technics
    • Similarly, SuFo cannot activate any Tech Advance skills (Normal Tech Advance, Tech Charge Advance, Tech JA Advance)
Using SuFo and SuTe for casting attack Tech along with pet is a bad idea! You'll end up with weak tech and weak pet!

About Critical Hits

While Su does not have JA, this is offset by pets having 70% minimum damage, as opposed to other weapon's 90% when using a ★13. Adding as much critical as possible allows pet to reach higher average damage, without compensating any aspects (maybe that 10 PP from 2 Spirit Canes).

Stack as many critical rate up as you can, it's a shortcut to high damage!

[[collapsible show="Show Simplified Calculation" hide="Hide Simplified Calculation"]]
By default, pet's minimum damage is roughly 70%, while Critical hits in PSO2 automatically put your damage to 100%. Thus, without any enhancements, your mean damage using a pet is:

(100% + 70%) / 2 = 85%

However, at any circumstances, you have at least 5% critical rate, which means 95% of time you deal average 85% damage, while the 5% of the time, you deal 100% of the damage.

95% * 85% + 5% * 100% = 85.75%

In other words, without any critical enhancements, averagely, you only do 85.75% damage.

Lets say you are using a Class Stance Critical (25%, assuming either Br or Bo sub) and a Critical Strike Ring Tech (20%), you will have a total of 50% Critical Rate (5% + 25% + 20%). Ignoring Critical Damage bonus from ring, your average damage will be:

50% * 85% + 50% * 100% = 92.5%

By boosting your critical rate to 50%, you gain 7.87% (relative to 85.75%) more damage.

What if you use all the critical option available without outside aid? Assuming Br or Bo sub, you already have 50% critical with ring (5% base + 25% stance + 20% ring). Add 14% from 2 Critical Candy Sticks and 20% from 2 Support Rolls. This will add up to 84% critical rate. Your average damage will be:

16% * 85% + 84% * 100% = 97.6%

You are almost about 14.82% (relative to 85.75%) more powerful than a non-critical build.

Example, a SuBr uses Deadly Parfait and maxed Critical Strike Tech ring: 84% critical rate and 103% * 110% = 113.3% damage during a critical hit (3% from Ring, 10% from Deadly Parfait). Their average damage will be:

16% * 85% + 84% * 113.3% = 108.77%

At more than 80% critical rate, the Deadly Parfait is more powerful than Super Complete Parfait (The damage rate with Super Complete Parfait alone will be 108.13%). And, with outside aid like Shifta Critical and Critical Field, pretty much 100% critical is guaranteed, bumping the overall damage to 113.3%

Icon Name Description
[[image ./img%3Apso2-tech/tech-li-resta.png class="pso2-icon double pixelate"]] Resta Heals all allied units in an area.Pet will request a Resta sympathy if they have a low HP.Preferred to have Brilliant craft (increases healing).
[[image ./img%3Apso2-tech/tech-li-anti.png class="pso2-icon double pixelate"]] Anti Restores status effect of all allied units in an area.A full-charged Anti lasts about 5 seconds on the field, you can use this as a preemptive move if you see a status move is incoming, like Elder's ice meteor.Preferred to have Concentrated craft (reduces charge time).
[[image ./img%3Apso2-tech/tech-fi-shifta.png class="pso2-icon double pixelate"]] Shifta Raises base attack power of all allied units in an area.Pet will request Shifta sympathy during battle.Pet needs to have the Shifta buff for increased attack; having Shifta buff on the character is irrelevant to pet's damage.Preferred to have Multi craft (more ticks).
[[image ./img%3Apso2-tech/tech-ic-deband.png class="pso2-icon double pixelate"]] Deband Raises base defense power of all allied units in an area.Deband is not as essential as Shifta, but is a key tech to have for Bo sub.Preferred to have Multi craft (more ticks).
[[image ./img%3Apso2-tech/tech-wi-zanverse.png class="pso2-icon double pixelate"]] Zanverse Inflicts additional 20% Wind damage when the pet is within the Zanverse radius.Best combined with long-range pets like Popple.Zanversed pet will affect the DoT given to enemy, as long as the pet is on the Zanverse area.Preferred to have Concentrated craft (reduces charge time).
[[image ./img%3Apso2-tech/tech-da-megiverse.png class="pso2-icon double pixelate"]] Megiverse Restores HP equal to 25% of damages inflicted if the pet is within the Megiverse radius.Note that since pet does the damage, character will not benefit from the skill at all, unless [[span class="icon op-pot"]]Sinister Stare (Glance of Darkness) is active.[[/span]]Either craft of Megiverse is fine.
[[image ./img%3Apso2-tech/tech-fi-safoie.png class="pso2-icon double pixelate"]] Safoie Type-0 Must have Type-0 Craft (available at start).A movement PA that helps you travel faster. It also tracks enemy's height, and has a lot of hits to help you escape from Fhange (that red-prison thing which traps you in an E-Trial).
[[image ./img%3Apso2-tech/tech-el-ilzonde.png class="pso2-icon double pixelate"]] Ilzonde An alternate movement PA if Safoie Type-0 is out of reach.Has a high PP cost, ditch this once you have Safoie-0.

Pets

The other important thing beside raising your pet properly is how to use them properly. There are a number of pets for a Summoner, each with their own specific purpose.

Glossary

Please note the following glossary before reading the detailed description of each pets.

Terms Description
DPS Rating Rating of Damage per second, calculated roughly by damage divided by frame, divided by average damage of Pet PAs. This is solely used to determine which pet attack is more powerful when used over and over. It does not mean that it is the most efficient attack.
Recall PA A Photon Arts (PA) that returns pet to your side and stops it from using further attack. This will pause the effect of Near Auto Target ring. Unless noted, pet will perform the move first before returning.
DoT Damage-over-time, inflicts small damage over a set amount of time. It is similar to Poison, but is not counted as a status effect, hence do not activate Chase Advance Plus. A DoT skill will sucessfully deliver damage if the first hit lands, even if the part is hidden or the pet got stunned. However, it will cancel if the affected part is destroyed, or pet is unsummoned.
Sinister Stare (Glance of Darkness) The potential icon on the DPS colum shows the DPS rating when Sinister Stare (Glance of Darkness) is used.
The DPS value is relative to another pet, use it only to compare one pet to another!

Marron (マロン Maron)

Description
[[image ./img%3Apso2-pet/pet-maron.png class="pso2-icon quadriple"]] A defensive pet with self-explosion ability. Marron is best used when your enemy is agressive and have a lot of multi-hit attacks, like Omega Masquerage.Once was popular pet before damage cap was implemented; with damage cap in place, Marron Strike's capped 1M damage does lower DPS that its required setup. Using Marron for Strike attack only will lower their DPS a lot; consider using the strike as a bonus damage and focus on using Curse and Break as primary DPS.Marron's size has 3 stages, which powers up their Strike: The 1st stage is default; Marron will always be on 1st stage if you summon them; the 2nd stage is reached after 3 hits, in which Marron becomes big; the 3rd stage is reached after 9 hits, in which Marron becomes even bigger with flames coming out of their body; you have 15 seconds to perform Marron strike before Marron explodes on your hand and reduce your HP to a fraction.Unlike Melon, Marron has limited use on regular EQs: its overreliance on Marron Strike 3 to do damage become it's main weakness; Marron's main combo (Curse-Break) is weaker than the standard of a Jinga.It's niche, however, is in solo "hard difficulty" quest which features multi-hit bosses, i.e. Phaleg, Omega Masquerade, and Shiva; In those quest, you can throw Marron Strike 3 in under 30s and swap to another Marron.Stunned Marron takes 60s to recover.
Personality Description
[[span class="rear-icon flag-na"]]Underdog[[/span]]逆境Adverse 117% damage if HP drops below 25%.This is always activated during Marron Strike, thus the preferred personality.
[[span class="rear-icon flag-na"]]Indefatigable[[/span]]やせ我慢 Fierce A chance to recover 18% of max HP when taking damage.
キュートCute ★14 only.Combines Underdog and Indefatigable, as well as having increased rare item drop rate.
Strength Weakness
Suitable against aggressive bossesSuitable to take on Phantom XQHighest HPCan shield character from damageHigh PP regain from normal attackHas a high-powered DoT attackHas a bouncing homing attack Suicide attack requires 30-60 seconds to set up, thus making it unsuitable for bosses that's not aggressive (i.e. almost all bosses are not aggressive, the only really aggressive ones are Omega Masquerade, Phaleg, Omega Hunar, and Mithra).Requires more than 1 Marron to properly take advantage of its suicide attackRecovers long from stunNot much use outside fighting aggressive bossSomewhat not aggressive, despite being a melee pet

Rappy (ラッピー)

Description
[[image ./img%3Apso2-pet/pet-rappy.png class="pso2-icon quadriple"]] An all-rounder pet, very friendly to newbies, although obtaining their eggs is not newbie friendly (Rare drop from ARKS Rappy).Rappy invokes the Magikarp Power: its stat before L120 are not impressive, and has 250 points to fill on each stat of Pet Plus; Level 100 and 120 Rappy has attack differences of almost 400 points.They notably have strongest normal attacks, albeit smaller hit box; this is both blessing and a curse since it is more accurate to hit a weak point, but easier to miss moving enemies.They are the only pet to have a healing PA.Rappy is the best pet to abuse Braver sub's Attack Advance: Stacking Attack Advance and Spirited Parfait turns Rappy's normal attack into a PA, essentially allowing you to win boss fights by just holding Normal Attack Button.

Redran (レドラン)

Description
[[image ./img%3Apso2-pet/pet-redran.png class="pso2-icon quadriple"]] A long-range pet that can tear multi-part enemies, such as Ragne and Vibras, quickly.On the reverse side, they also can tear down Redran quickly.Redran has both the highest ATK among all pets, and one of the lowest DEF, with about 120 HP less than Synchro and only 60 DEF better.Redran, can jam: pressing a PA button at the same time when they lose target will cause them to skip the said PA, but will still cost PP!Redran has minimal use on EQ outside seasonal, defense, and endless quests; especially because they tend to run out of PP quickly.In addition, Redran is hard-pressed to secure the number of kills it needed in UH fields, further hampering its usage.
Personality Description
[[span class="rear-icon flag-na"]]Rambunctious[[/span]]あばれんぼうRowdy Raises damage by 2% for each enemy killed by Redran; capped at 50% or 150% damage total.The bonus will be reset upon entering campship and unsummoning Redran.This would be the preferred personality.
[[span class="rear-icon flag-na"]]Belligerent[[/span]]とうそうしんHawkish Raises damage depending on number of enemies near the Redran.106% for 1-4 enemies, 112% for 5 enemies and above.Since Redran is a long-range pet that has a low durability, this skill becomes counterproductive for its survival, specially since it does not do much in boss EQs.
ロックRock ★14 only.Combines Rambunctious and Belligerent, as well as having increased rare item drop rate.
Strength Weakness
Highest possible damage multiplier (150%) from personalityDecimates enemy with multiple parts quicklyHigh-powered normal attacksHigh ATKRecall attack has invulnerability frames Unsuitable for newbies.Prone to jammingBeside recall, all other attacks are slowLow HPLow DefNot much use against bosses that don't have multiple partsLittle use during Boss EQ

Vulcan (シンクロウ Synchro)

Description
[[image ./img%3Apso2-pet/pet-vulcan.png class="pso2-icon quadriple"]] An evolution of Shinkuro, but behaves on the opposite side.Vulcan is slow and emphasizes quality over quantity.Stat-wise, lesser power than Synchro, but a lot bulkier.Setup is easier as it does not require a stunned pet.
Personality Description
[[span class="rear-icon flag-na"]]Thoughtful[[/span]]なかま思いDevoted Similar to Shinkuro's personalityOnly available if you do rarity upgrade from a Shinkuro.
[[span class="rear-icon flag-na"]]Sly[[/span]]こうかつCunning Similar to Shinkuro's personalityOnly available if you do rarity upgrade from a Shinkuro.
ジェントルGentle Similar to Shinkuro's personalityOnly available if you do rarity upgrade from a Shinkuro.
アグレッシブAggressive Vulcan only.116% critical damage and 70% damage reduction, but reduces critical rate by 50%.Typically candies gives you 34% critical rate, on top of 5% default, thus your base critical rate is 39%; With 200 PP Phantom sub and a Critical Strike Ring, you gain another 60%, totalling 99%; offset by this personality's -50%, you'll end up with 49%, which is less than desirable.In order to increase your crit rate further wihout external help, you'll need 300 PP Ph sub for extra 20% rate, S6 Wise Skill (妙技の巧) for 15%; with the grand total of 84%.
Strength Weakness
Long attack animations benefits natural PP recovery.PAs have higher multiplier to compensate low ATK.High-powered normal attacks70% damage reductionNigh unkillable with 3000 HP, 2000 Def, and Powerful area attack with low cost Unsuitable for newbies.Introduces the concept of timing which previously only applicable to Changed Viola and Wanda/Jinga SlicersSlow PA animation, most of which put the stong attacks at the very end of said animation.Requires chaining different PAs to maximize damageRequires 7 different PAs to activate it's strongest attack, 3 more than Synchro.Low PP regain from normal attacksNo sound cue for maximum chain.All things combined, it has unecessary complexity that hinders it's usage.
